item: 1.12 — a finished thinking body does not paint the CLI's trailing newlines (2026-10-08)
branch: thinkBlock() trims the thinking text before it becomes the <details> body. The body is `white-space: pre-wrap` (the only block that keeps the model's own line breaks), so a trailing newline paints as an empty line and the gap below an OPENED thought reads as --block-gap plus one or two blank lines.
provenance: MEASURED 2026-10-08 across the 40 most recent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects (CLI 2.1.270 – 2.1.293): every persisted `thinking` block with text — 13 of 13 — ends with exactly two newlines; none starts with whitespace. The live `thinking_delta` frames concatenate to the same string (the transcript IS that concatenation). The official VS Code webview renders `$.thinking` through its markdown renderer, where trailing newlines vanish for free; the panel's .body is plain pre-wrap text, so they paint (user screenshot 2026-10-08: an opened 'Thought for 1s' followed by a visibly larger gap before the next Edit line). Frame shapes copied from fixture 19 (message_start / content_block_start thinking / thinking_delta / content_block_stop). NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-10-08 against the sandbox still serving the pre-change webview (started before the edit): 3 passed, 3 failed — the three GUARD asserts passed, the three DISCRIMINATING asserts failed; the body kept its two trailing newlines and measured 40px opened against 20px for the trimmed reference (line-height 20.15px at 13px) — one empty line, the <details> 68px vs 48px. Fixed build: 6/6.
